standard.title: 12- and 24-hour time
standard.description: Compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and solve practical problems involving the conversion between them
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can calculate durations and work with am/pm time (AC9M4M03). They have not yet compared the two systems structurally or converted systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and solve practical problems involving conversion between them.

nodes.label: Comparing the two systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the structural difference between 12- and 24-hour time and explain why 24-hour time is used in some contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the key difference between the systems; read a given time in both formats.
nodes.typical_width: Compare the two systems across a full 24-hour cycle; identify where confusion arises (12:00 noon/midnight, 13:00 onwards); explain why 24-hour time is unambiguous.
wider: Investigate professions that use 24-hour time (transport, military, medicine) and why
Explore time zones and how 24-hour notation avoids am/pm ambiguity across zones
success_criteria: Student reads a given time correctly in both 12- and 24-hour format
Student explains the structural advantage of 24-hour notation

nodes.label: Converting between systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can convert times between 12- and 24-hour systems, including times after noon and around midnight.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert a given am or pm time to 24-hour notation and vice versa; demonstrate correct handling of noon and midnight.
nodes.typical_width: Solve conversion problems across a full cycle including edge cases (12:00am, 12:00pm, 00:00); apply in practical contexts (timetables, schedules).
wider: Read and interpret real transport timetables in 24-hour time

response_modes.reason: Conversion accuracy requires internalising the +12/-12 rule for pm times with the noon/midnight exception. This is a precision skill where targeted practice reduces systematic errors.
The noon/midnight edge cases (12:00am = 00:00, 12:00pm = 12:00) are persistent misconceptions. Multiple contexts exposing these cases help students build correct mental models.

nodes.hinge_reason: Conversion accuracy is the prerequisite for Node 3 — students with noon/midnight errors produce systematically wrong duration calculations when times span these boundaries.
success_criteria: Student converts between systems correctly including noon and midnight
Student applies conversions to read a practical timetable

nodes.label: Solving duration problems with 24-hour time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can calculate durations using 24-hour time and solve practical scheduling problems.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate the duration between two times given in 24-hour format; solve a simple scheduling problem.
nodes.typical_width: Solve multi-step duration problems using 24-hour times; calculate arrival times, departure times and durations from timetables; handle problems that cross midnight.
wider: Interpret real transport timetables and plan multi-leg journeys
Calculate time differences across time zones using 24-hour notation

response_modes.reason: Duration calculation with 24-hour times requires consistent application of the subtraction process; errors at midnight-crossing cluster here and need targeted practice.

success_criteria: Student calculates a duration between two 24-hour times correctly
Student solves a practical scheduling problem using 24-hour time
